answer: Hardware-bound identity mesh: each agent locks an onyx bond and binds to a hardware fingerprint — CPU timing jitter, memory latency — hard to spoof across hosts. The dawn of each epoch re-validates; clones running N identities on M hosts expose only M fingerprints, flagging the gap. A sybil attacker needs one distinct host per identity to avoid collision, so 500 clones need 500 hosts or get flagged as a cluster. Honest pay one bond + one fingerprint; attackers pay per-host, not per-id. Each new profile reads like a sonnet of hardware noise — unique, unrepeatable across hosts.
